•
Revenue recognition: Apply ASC 606 to new and amended contracts, including performance obligations, standalone selling price allocation, contract modifications, and variable consideration for usage-based fees.

•
Month-end and quarter-end close: Prepare revenue entries, deferred revenue schedules, and contract-level reconciliations on a predictable close calendar.

•
Systems and data integrity: Maintain the sub-ledger flow between HubSpot and Rillet, reconcile contract data to revenue schedules, and flag gaps before they reach the close.

Audit readiness: Build and maintain support for revenue and deferred revenue balances, draft technical memos, and respond to auditor requests.

Process improvement: Document procedures, tighten controls, and automate manual steps so the function scales without adding headcount at the same pace.

•
Cross-functional partnership: Explain revenue implications in plain language to non-finance teams and help reduce close-time fire drills.

Your Profile

• Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA or CPA-eligible preferred.

• 4-6 years of revenue accounting experience in public accounting and/or a high-growth SaaS company.

• Hands-on ASC 606 experience with multi-element and usage-based contracts, including SSP analysis and contract modifications.

• Experience owning a revenue close, including deferred revenue roll-forwards and reconciliations.

• Comfort with cloud ERP and billing systems (Rillet experience a plus) and strong Excel or Google Sheets skills.

• Clear communicator who can explain GAAP to Sales, Legal, and executive stakeholders.

• Detail-oriented and proactive, with a bias toward improving the process, not only running it.

• B2B SaaS experience, ideally MedTech or another regulated vertical.

• Usage-based or hybrid pricing experience and the related ASC 606 implications.

• Experience with ASC 340-40 deferred commissions.

• Familiarity with HubSpot CRM and its integration to a revenue sub-ledger.

• Exposure to SOX scoping or public company readiness work.

This role involves getting hands-on with a device, opening it up, and proving what an attacker with physical or local access can really do.

title: AI Research Engineer (New York)
description:
ABOUT EDRA

Edra is solving one of the hardest problems in enterprise AI: AI models are generic but company processes are specific. We build AI agents that learn how processes actually run, and then run their operations.

We're a Series A startup, backed by Sequoia and other leading VC firms, led by Co-Founders who created and led Forward Deployed AI Engineering at Palantir, and we're growing our team in New York and London. We're a deeply technical team of engineers, AI researchers, and strategists with a high bar for talent and a shared belief that exceptional people are the foundation of everything great we'll build.

THE ROLE

We're building a learning system that teaches AI agents how enterprises actually work. Our system starts from what a customer already has: knowledge base articles, support conversations, tickets, system logs, and agent traces. From that evidence it reverse-engineers how the business actually runs and writes the process down as instructions a person can inspect and an agent can execute, with confidence scoring to know when to automate and when to seek human input.

We're looking for AI Research Engineers who have built complex, production LLM-based systems. Whether you've scaled LLM workflows handling millions of requests, built multi-agent systems in production, or designed evaluation frameworks for enterprise deployments, we want people who bring intensity and self-direction to their craft. You'll work on our agentic learning environment: the loops that turn human corrections and agent outcomes into better knowledge and instructions over time. The job combines applied research with ownership of production systems. You find a failure, form a hypothesis, run the experiment, and ship the fix into real customer workflows.

You'll spend most of your time advancing our core context-learning library and the harness that powers our agents across every customer. The work spans continuous learning, context engineering, agent orchestration, and evaluation. You'll contribute to our knowledge benchmarks and to the self-improving capabilities of the harness.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Build and extend our core context-learning library, turning customer-informed problems into reusable platform capabilities.

- Design and implement LLM-powered systems and agentic workflows from concept to production.

- Build agentic features for knowledge management: agents that can edit, update, and maintain large knowledge bases autonomously.

- Build continuous learning loops that use human corrections and production outcomes to find knowledge gaps, detect changed procedures, and improve prompts and instructions.

- Build reliability and confidence systems: evaluation frameworks, confidence scoring, and logic for when to automate and when to escalate to a human.

- Architect async, scalable systems that handle complex AI orchestration.

- Contribute to the direction of our AI strategy and product capabilities.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

- You've built a complex, production LLM system with real depth: multiple layers of engineering decisions you can walk through, including what changed after real users arrived.

- You have practical depth in one or more of context engineering, retrieval, agent orchestration, memory, evaluation, or learning from feedback.

- You have experimental judgment. You can turn an ambiguous problem into a testable hypothesis, set a baseline, and tell a real improvement from noise.

- You're excited by open-ended problems where the solution might not exist yet.

- You can navigate between research papers and production code with equal comfort.

- You're a strong communicator who can explain your work to teammates and customers.

- You have 3+ years of professional experience.

 

Don’t meet all of the above traits? We’d still love to hear from you. We’re looking for exceptional people with unique skills and interests, and we know that great people have different backgrounds and skillsets.

﻿The Company
Sunbit builds financial technology for real life. Our AI-native platform helps more people get to “yes” at the moments that matter with personalized offers, transparent terms, and no added consumer fees. In stores, practices and service centers across the country, Sunbit provides a fast, fair pay-over-time option. For everything else, the Sunbit Credit Card delivers a modern, no-fee credit experience managed in a powerful mobile app.
We are guided by people-centered values: Serve Others Before Self, Include Always, Connect Genuinely, Innovate for Good. These values shape how we build, how we support customers and merchants, and how we work with each other.
What makes Sunbit different is an AI-native infrastructure that runs through the full customer and merchant journey. Our interconnected AI systems power instant decisioning, streamline fraud checks with human-in-the-loop safeguards, and enable highly personalized offers at scale. The result is a quick, fair, and simple experience for consumers and merchants.
We pair this technology with inclusion and transparency. Sunbit delivers industry-leading approval rates - 90%+ in auto service and 85%+ in dental - while maintaining zero consumer fee-based revenue. It is a better way to serve people and merchants, proven at scale.
Today, Sunbit is available across a nationwide, in-person merchant network of 30,000+ locations spanning auto service centers, dental and optical practices, veterinary clinics, and other specialty services. We help teams say “yes” more often and help customers move forward with confidence.
The Role:
We are looking for a hands-on Director of Analytics to lead Merchant Ecosystem analytics. You will manage a team of senior analysts and work directly with Merchant and company leaders.
The role has two halves. First, you will own analytics self-serve: moving us from a model where business teams ask analysts for answers, to a governed, agent-enabled environment where they answer their own questions with data they trust. Second, you will own merchant and BNPL analytics, including the loan application funnel and loan performance.
You do not need a lending background. If you are strong on funnel analytics and self-serve, we will teach you the BNPL domain.
Requirements
What you’ll do:

•
Own analytics self-serve. Lead the move from analyst-led reporting to governed self-service, and set the adoption targets you report on.

•
Own the semantic layer. Own the certified metric layer in Snowflake that both Sigma and AI agents query, so the same question always returns the same answer. Decide what gets certified and who approves changes.

•
Put analytics agents into real use. Work with Data Engineering, Product, and AI/ML to give business teams conversational analytics. Choose the use cases, set the guardrails, and drive adoption past the pilot stage.

•
Govern AI-assisted analysis. Set accuracy checks, review thresholds, and escalation paths. Measure agent answer quality the way you would measure a model.

•
Own the BNPL application funnel. Build the trusted view of the loan journey: application starts, drop-off, decision outcomes, approval and take rates, funding, and loan performance. Find the friction, and work with Product, Credit, and Engineering to remove it.

•
Own merchant lifecycle performance. Measure how merchants are acquired, activated, and retained across our verticals. Define what a healthy merchant looks like, and what predicts the ones that stall.

•
Set the standard for evidence. Own merchant KPI definitions, and run the experimentation practice: A/B tests, incrementality reads, and elasticity studies.

•
Lead the team and advise executives. Manage, coach analysts. Act as the analytics partner to Merchant and company leadership. Expect about 30-40% of your time to be your own hands-on analysis.
